matchstick.title: Move vertical I-stick between numerals
matchstick.principle: Transfer a single vertical stick that forms an I from one numeral to another to adjust their values while preserving valid numeral forms.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation is close to being correct and a vertical stick from an I could increase or decrease a numeral's value without breaking either numeral.
matchstick.example: Detaching a vertical stick from an I and leaving the original numeral without any I, resulting in an invalid numeral.

matchstick.title: Prefer intra-character stick relocation
matchstick.principle: First explore moving a stick within the same character (e.g., turning X into V or I into L) before considering moves between characters.
matchstick.when_to_apply: At the start of solving, before trying inter‑character moves, examine each character to see if moving a stick inside it can produce a different valid numeral.
matchstick.example: Skipping the possibility of turning X into V and instead moving a stick to another character, missing a simpler solution.

matchstick.title: Validate symbols after stick move
matchstick.principle: After moving a stick, check that both the source and destination symbols remain valid Roman numerals or operators.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Immediately after any stick relocation, before evaluating the arithmetic.
matchstick.example: Moving a diagonal from an X and leaving a single diagonal, which is not a valid Roman numeral.

matchstick.title: Avoid single angled sticks
matchstick.principle: Never leave a lone diagonal stick as a standalone character; V and X must consist of two diagonal sticks.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever a diagonal stick is removed from a character, ensure the resulting character still contains two diagonals.
matchstick.example: Creating a lone diagonal stick as a character, which does not correspond to any Roman numeral.

matchstick.title: Convert plus to minus by removing vertical stick
matchstick.principle: Turn a plus sign into a minus sign by detaching its vertical stick; the removed stick can then be used elsewhere.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a plus sign is present and a vertical stick could be useful for adjusting a numeral.
matchstick.example: Removing the vertical stick from a plus sign but forgetting to use it, leaving the plus sign unchanged and the stick lost.

matchstick.title: Create new numeral by reordering stick
matchstick.principle: A detached stick can be placed as a separate character to form a new numeral (e.g., adding a vertical stick creates an I).
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a stick is removed and there is empty space where a new valid numeral could be placed.
matchstick.example: Placing a detached stick in isolation, forming an invalid shape that is not a recognized numeral.

matchstick.title: Consider inter-character stick relocation
matchstick.principle: If no intra‑character move yields a valid equality, explore moving a stick from one character to another.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After exhausting all intra‑character possibilities without finding a solution.
matchstick.example: Only trying intra‑character moves and overlooking a solution that requires moving a stick from one numeral to another.

matchstick.title: Swap operators via horizontal stick move
matchstick.principle: Move a horizontal stick from the equals sign to a minus sign (or vice versa) to swap the operators.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation contains both '=' and '-' and a horizontal stick can be transferred between them.
matchstick.example: Swapping '=' and '-' but not recomputing the arithmetic, leading to an equation that still doesn't hold.

matchstick.title: Augment numeral with vertical stick from operator
matchstick.principle: When converting a plus sign to a minus sign by removing its vertical stick, attach that stick to a numeral to increase its value.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After turning '+' into '-', look for a numeral that can accept an extra vertical stick (e.g., turning I into II).
matchstick.example: Attaching a vertical stick from a plus sign to a numeral that already has a vertical, resulting in an invalid shape.

matchstick.title: Verify arithmetic after stick move
matchstick.principle: After forming new Roman numerals and operators, compute their numeric values to ensure the equation holds.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After any transformation that yields a syntactically valid equation.
matchstick.example: Accepting a visually correct equation without checking that the numeric values actually match.

matchstick.description: Overlooking intra‑character transformations (e.g., X→V) before inter‑character moves
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model tends to consider moving sticks between characters first, missing simpler solutions that involve reshaping a single character.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always explore intra‑character stick relocations (such as turning X into V or I into L) before trying inter‑character moves.

matchstick.description: Assuming sticks retain their orientation and not rotating horizontals to verticals (or vice versa) when repositioning
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model may incorrectly treat a horizontal stick as interchangeable with a vertical one, violating the puzzle's orientation constraints.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Preserve the original orientation of each stick when moving it; a horizontal stick must remain horizontal, a vertical must remain vertical, and diagonals must stay diagonal.

matchstick.description: Not evaluating the arithmetic result after each candidate transformation
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model may focus on making the symbols valid without checking whether the resulting equation is numerically correct.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After any stick move, compute the numeric values of both sides and verify that the equality holds.

matchstick.description: Assuming operator swaps (e.g., = ↔ -) automatically solve the puzzle
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model may think that swapping operators will always balance the equation, ignoring the numeric impact.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: When swapping operators, also recompute the arithmetic to ensure the new equation is true.

matchstick.description: Ignoring the I↔L transformation (adding/removing a horizontal stick to/from an I)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model overlooks the possibility of turning an I into an L (or vice versa) by adding or removing a horizontal stick, missing potential solutions.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Consider the I↔L transformation as a valid intra‑character move when a horizontal stick is available.
